correctness.rationale: Reversibility makes Delta=I-P selfadjoint on l²(pi); Delta s=0 and <s,e>=a=sqrt(pi_w). If exact unit success, final state is a phase multiple of e, and commuting time evolution with H forces equality of first and second moments of s and e. First moment fixes gamma=(1-a²)/(1-r); second gives ||Delta e||²=(1-r)²/(1-a²). Cauchy–Schwarz between e-a*s and Delta e is saturated; its equality case implies Delta e=kappa(e-a*s) with kappa=(1-r)/(1-a²), equivalent coordinatewise to constant entrance. Conversely that identity implies H*s=-a e and H*e=-a s at gamma*, so invariant span{s,e} yields evolution cos(at)s+i sin(at)e, exact probability and all perfect times. Independently tested exact reversible weighted networks including cone-over-path with pi_w=1/3, P_uw=1/2 and asymmetric triangle that fails. Restricted to finite irreducible chains pi_w∈(0,1), gamma>0; no conclusions on approximation or nonreversible walks.
residual_risks: Scope limited to precisely stated hypotheses; finite replay never independently proves infinite or geometric statement.
